questions.q: What was Bellhaven's starting point at the beginning of this capstone, before any changes were made?
options: One database, BellhavenOLTP, on one unprotected server, SQLPRD01, with only a nightly full backup
Two datacenters already connected via log shipping
A three-replica Availability Group already in place but untested
A Failover Cluster Instance with no backup strategy
questions.explain: The capstone opened with a single, unprotected server and a nightly-full-backup-only baseline — everything else was built across the following lessons.

questions.q: Which two ruled-out alternatives did AG_Bellhaven's design have to be defended against?
options: Two separate, unrelated Availability Groups
Database mirroring and replication
A Failover Cluster Instance and log shipping alone
SIMPLE recovery model and BULK_LOGGED recovery model
questions.explain: Lesson 42 ruled out an FCI (shared storage doesn't survive site loss) and log shipping alone (too slow for the local RTO) in favor of one AG spanning both roles.

questions.q: What specifically did Lesson 45's and Lesson 46's tests prove, that a description of the configuration alone wouldn't?
options: Nothing new — the tests were purely a formality
That AG_Bellhaven's syntax was typed correctly
That the failover time and data-loss window were actually measured under real test conditions, not just assumed from the design
That Bellhaven's business requirements were unrealistic
questions.explain: The tests turned assumed RTO/RPO numbers into measured, verified results — the core difference between a design and a proven system, per this lesson.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the strongest way to present this capstone as a portfolio project in an interview?
options: Focus only on the T-SQL syntax used to create the AG
Walk through the stated requirement, the decision defended against alternatives, the implementation, and the measured results from the two tests
Avoid mentioning the forced-failover disaster test since it involved data loss
Simply state that Availability Groups were used, without further detail
questions.explain: The lesson frames the strongest story as the full arc: requirement, defended decision, implementation, and measured test results — not just naming the technology used.

questions.q: Which three other courses complete the Advanced stage of the SQL Server Database Administrator path alongside this one?
options: Data Engineering Foundations, Databricks & Delta Lake, and Fabric & Real-Time Analytics
SQL Server Performance Tuning, Azure Database Administrator, and PowerShell Automation & DevOps for DBAs
Tableau, Advanced Excel, and Git/GitHub/CI-CD
T-SQL Fundamentals, SQL Server Database Development and BI, and Data Warehousing
questions.explain: The lesson names the Advanced stage as four courses: SQL Server Performance Tuning (complete), this HA/DR course, Azure Database Administrator, and PowerShell Automation & DevOps for DBAs.
